items.stem: Why can a growing, profitable company still face a cash crisis?

options.text: Growth ties up cash in receivables and inventory faster than profit converts to cash
options.rationale: Correct: rapid growth absorbs working capital.

options.text: Because profit and cash are legally required to be equal
options.rationale: They are not required to be equal.

options.text: Because depreciation uses up cash each month

items.explanation: Correct: rapid growth absorbs working capital.

items.stem: Which TWO actions shorten the cash conversion cycle? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: faster collection reduces days sales outstanding.

options.text: Negotiating longer payment terms with suppliers
options.rationale: Correct: longer payables terms extend the cash held.
Paying early shortens payables and uses cash sooner.

items.explanation: Correct: faster collection reduces days sales outstanding.

items.stem: A 13-week cash forecast is most useful because it:

options.text: Shows the timing of receipts and payments so a shortfall can be anticipated and managed
options.rationale: Correct: it is about timing, not period profit.

options.text: Replaces the need for an annual budget
options.rationale: It complements, not replaces, the budget.

options.text: Guarantees the company will not run out of cash
options.rationale: It informs decisions but guarantees nothing.
It is a short-term liquidity tool.

items.explanation: Correct: it is about timing, not period profit.
